messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — Okta alerted on ~18 accounts with concurrent logins across EU + US within 30m. Flagged as high-risk (impossible travel style). Alert IDs: 4928-4936. Anyone seeing related tickets?
Okta Bot: Okta Alert: event_type=impossible_travel, users=18, risk_score>70. Suggested actions: revoke_sessions, force_mfa, lock_account.
Mina Patel: I'll start revoking sessions for the highest-risk users. Jordan, can you check VPN/proxy egress and partner tunnels?
Jordan Reyes: On it. Quick grep shows many auths coming from same ASN (AS13335) — Cloudflare WARP/egress pool. Could be partner VPN or a misconfigured SSO proxy.
Alex Chen: For containment: (1) revoke sessions for affected users, (2) force MFA prompt on next auth, (3) temporarily tighten geo rules for new locations, (4) capture Okta audit and KMS logs.
Mina Patel: Revoking sessions now for top 6 users. Running:
```
# revoke sessions via okta cli
okta sessions revoke --user alice@example.com --confirm
```
SRE Bot: Observability: we pushed throttling rules to auth gateway — small latency bump expected. Notifying infra.
Jordan Reyes: Confirmed IPs map to Cloudflare WARP + several corporate VPN exits. Reaching out to infra + partner ops.
Alex Chen: Also check for MFA fatigue pattern — many rapid retries then a success. If we see that, treat as potential social engineering or coerced auth. Add detection rule.
Mina Patel: KMS audit: spotted 2 decrypt operations by service-account "analytics-runner" at 02:14 and 02:27 UTC, outside normal window. Tagging for follow-up.
Jordan Reyes: SIEM query I'm running:
```
index=okta_events "impossible_travel" OR event.outcome=failed_mfa | stats count by user, src_ip, geo | where count>3
```
Alex Chen: Communications: do NOT send customer-facing security notices yet. Notify CISO + legal + support privately. Schedule incident postmortem in 24h.
Mina Patel: Created detection ticket SEC-4567 for MFA fatigue pattern and lockout spikes. Also increasing lockout sensitivity to 5 failed MFA attempts within 10m.
Okta Bot: Action completed: 6 sessions revoked, 12 users forced to re-auth with MFA, 2 accounts temporarily locked.
Alex Chen: Jordan — once SIEM consolidates, produce a CSV of affected users and share in the secure incident bucket. Also export full Okta audit for the window. Rotate any plaintext API keys we find in use.
Jordan Reyes: Uploading artifacts: s3://redwood-sec-incident/1752007890/okta-audit.log.gpg and s3://redwood-sec-incident/1752007890/siem-queries.txt.gpg
Mina Patel: Follow-ups: schedule RBAC review for admin accounts used during incident, rotate service-account keys, add KMS key-usage logging (enable more granular audit), and add a rule to detect "session revoke count > 5 in 1h".
Alex Chen: Agreed. We'll also add a short runbook section for partner VPN-related SSO anomalies. Postmortem owners: Mina (containment timeline), Jordan (log analysis), Alex (communications + follow-ups).
Mina Patel: I'll update the runbook and set a calendar invite for the postmortem in 24h.
Alex Chen: Thanks all. Keep this channel updated with any escalation. Closing thread once postmortem invite is accepted. :thumbsup:
